title: Evaluation Resolution Confounds Learning-Rule Comparisons in Model-Brain RSA of Early Visual Cortex
abstract: arXiv:2608.12408v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Representational similarity analysis (RSA) is increasingly used to ask which learning rules give convolutional networks brain-like representations. Because biologically plausible rules such as feedback alignment, predictive coding and STDP do not scale, studies that include them train small networks on small images (typically 32x32 CIFAR) and then compare them to brain responses modeled at much higher resolution. We find that a common result in this setting, that untrained or locally trained networks rival or beat backpropagation at early visual cortex, depends strongly on the resolution at which the network is evaluated. The V1 gap between an untrained network and a backpropagation-trained one widens from -0.001 +/- 0.007 at the 32px training resolution to +0.044 +/- 0.006 at 224px, growing monotonically across six resolutions (n=5 seeds). translated_title: 评估分辨率混淆了模型-大脑RSA中学习规则比较的结果（早期视觉皮层研究）
translated_abstract: 表征相似性分析（RSA）越来越多地被用于探究哪些学习规则能使卷积网络产生类似大脑的表征。由于生物学上合理的学习规则（如反馈对齐、预测编码和STDP）难以扩展，包含这些规则的研究通常在小图像（典型为32x32的CIFAR）上训练小型网络，然后将其与以更高分辨率建模的大脑反应进行比较。我们发现，在这种设置下的一个常见结果——即未训练或局部训练的网络在早期视觉皮层上能与反向传播相媲美甚至超越——强烈依赖于网络评估时的分辨率。未训练网络与反向传播训练网络之间的V1差距从32像素训练分辨率下的-0.001 ± 0.007扩大到224像素下的+0.044 ± 0.006，并在六种分辨率下单调增长（n=5个种子）。这一结果在人类fMRI数据中成立，并且在方向上也在单种子猕猴电生理数据中成立，沿着t...
tldr: 本文发现，在模型-大脑RSA比较中，评估分辨率的选择会显著影响不同学习规则（如未训练/局部训练与反向传播）在早期视觉皮层上的表现排名，高分辨率评估下反向传播的优势更明显，提示现有比较结果可能受分辨率混淆影响。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that evaluation resolution significantly confounds comparisons of learning rules in model-brain RSA, with backpropagation's advantage over untrained/local networks in early visual cortex widening at higher resolutions, suggesting prior results may be resolution-dependent.
